A website for a law firm that works with fintech companies, from licensing and corporate law to fraud and asset recovery. The client wanted a site as distinctive as their practice, inspired by neon lights and the digital world, that still feels professional.

My role

A new website, built from zero

I designed the website at Saphira Agency, working with our design team lead and a project manager. The firm had no site to build on, so the visual language and the page structure were created together, from the homepage to the blog, articles and service pages.

Challenge

A law firm that shouldn't look like one

The client works where law meets finance and technology. A classic law-firm website would not reflect that, but the site still had to earn the trust a legal practice needs.

  1. 01

    Distinctive, but professional

    The brief asked for neon and the digital world. The design had to bring that energy without turning a legal practice into a nightclub poster.

  2. 02

    Expertise at a glance

    The firm covers six practice areas, from IT law to fraud and asset recovery. A visitor had to understand what the firm does within the first scroll.

  3. 03

    Works on every device

    The layout had to hold together on computers, tablets and phones.

Deep dive 01

Neon, held in place by a grid

The visual concept balances two things: bright, glowing color and a strict, quiet structure.

  1. 01

    A gradient for every page

    Each page opens with its own gradient, from magenta and deep blue on the homepage to teal on the blog. A layer of grain keeps the colors soft, closer to light than to plastic. It gives every page its own character inside one system.

  2. 02

    Thin lines as structure

    1px lines run through every page and divide it into columns. They frame the bright gradients and keep long pages calm and ordered.

  1. 03

    Wide type, light text

    Headings are set in Syne Bold capitals and end with a pink full stop. Body text is Helvetica Light. The palette is four colors: a warm graphite instead of pure black, sand for labels, pink for actions and an off-white for text.

Deep dive 02

Interactions that invite you to explore

Motion was part of the design from the start: the site should feel alive and reward curiosity, while staying easy to read.

  1. 01

    Practice areas that light up

    On hover, a practice-area card fills with its own gradient, the title gets a pink highlight and an arrow appears. The grid stays calm until you interact with it.

  2. 02

    Small rewards for curiosity

    The "Learn more" circle splits into three rings on hover, the outlined "Contact us" button fills with pink, and headings reveal line by line as you scroll.
